Gujarat's own e-procurement platform (nProcure, operated for the state by (n)Code Solutions) could not be reached from this network, so its coverage row is unverified rather than negative.

Five awards: two MSEDCL renewable LoAs to Tata Power, one MSEDCL solar PPA to Adani Green, and two Samruddhi Mahamarg EPC packages. Of the 16 Samruddhi packages awarded by MSRDC in January 2019 across 13 contractors, only 2 went to companies in the 259-company ICIP universe. No sourced value for any Maharashtra award.

Four awards, all four groups of one project - the Ganga Expressway. This is the only in-scope state where the awarding authority itself publishes concessionaire names alongside rupee amounts, which is why UP is the only state here with values on every row.

Two power-procurement awards, both to central PSU subsidiaries (SJVN, NLC India) rather than to private developers. The SJVN row is the only one in the file with a company-stated project cost and a stated auction date.
Four awards: the three 250 MW Rewa Ultra Mega Solar allocations of 2017 and one MPRDC road package. None of the three Rewa winners was itself a listed company. No values sourced.

Two limestone block auctions, both won by UltraTech Cement, both in the same tehsil (Chittapur, Kalburgi). Both are documented via the company's own stock-exchange disclosures, and in both the winning premium percentage - the actual price - is absent.

Three awards, all three winners of one TNGECL battery storage auction. One of the three is in the ICIP universe. SIPCOT displays major-allottee logos and runs land allotment dashboards but does not publish company-level allotment records.

Three land allotments taken from APIIC's own published SEZ allotment tables. APIIC is the only in-scope state agency found publishing company-level allotments; it publishes name, plot, extent and activity but no date and no price.

ZERO awards captured. Not because nothing was awarded - press reporting records TGIIC issuing land allotment orders to 70 companies in one month and to 113 firms in another - but because Telangana publishes those as aggregate counts and rupee investment totals without naming the allottees. Telangana is the clearest example in this file of a state where the award record exists but is not public.

Five awards: four iron ore blocks to JSW Steel from the 2020 auction round, and the OERC-awarded central Odisha distribution concession to Tata Power. Not one has a sourced rupee value or a per-block premium percentage. Tata Power holds three further Odisha discom concessions not captured here for want of a fetchable primary source.
One award: the state's acquisition and transfer of land for Adani Power's Godda plant. No consideration published. This is a land transfer effected on request, not a competitive process.
One award: the Gare Pelma Sector III MDO contract to Adani Enterprises. Its value is withheld; the State Information Commission ordered disclosure in 2019 and we could not verify compliance.

ZERO awards captured. WBIDC runs a public land allotment dashboard, but it publishes application counts and available plot areas only - no allottee names, no prices, no dates. Press reporting of a CAG finding on a WBIDC land allotment to a Flipkart logistics entity could not be fetched and is recorded as a gap, not an award.

gaps: THE HEADLINE FINDING: not one of the 13 in-scope states publishes a queryable or downloadable register of awarded contracts. Eight state portals were fetched and confirmed running the same NIC GePNIC build (v1.09.23); all eight expose awarded-contract information only tender-by-tender through a web UI, with no API, no bulk export and no open-data dataset. Five more (Gujarat, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh) could not be reached from this network and none is known to publish such data either. Every award in this file was reconstructed from the WINNER's disclosures or from trade press - not from the awarding state. State procurement in India is, for research purposes, effectively unindexed.

Bidder counts are absent for 100% of awards (0 of 37). No state, sector or process type in this file discloses how many parties bid. soleBidder is consequently null nearly everywhere, and no claim about competitiveness of any state process can be supported from this dataset.

Rupee values are absent for 32 of 37 awards. The only state that published amounts alongside concessionaire names was UPEIDA, and what it published is the VGF grant, not the bid value or project cost.

Mineral auction prices are systematically missing. The economically meaningful number in a state mineral auction is the winning premium percentage over the IBM-notified price. It is absent from all six mining awards here (four Odisha iron ore, two Karnataka limestone), including from the winners' own stock-exchange filings. MSTC hosts the auctions but publishes tender documents only - no results or preferred-bidder register.

Land allotment prices are absent for all six land awards (Khavda x2, APIIC x3, Godda). For Khavda this means roughly 28,500 hectares of state land across two allottees, and about 72,400 hectares across all six developers, with no published price per hectare anywhere we could find.

MDO (mine developer and operator) contract values are withheld as a matter of practice. The Chhattisgarh State Information Commission had to order disclosure of the Gare Pelma III agreement in July 2019 after an RTI refusal; the same source records Rajasthan and Maharashtra also refusing. We did not verify whether the Chhattisgarh order was complied with.

Telangana: zero company-level awards sourceable. TGIIC land allotments are announced in aggregate ('70 companies', '113 firms', rupee investment totals) with no allottee register. This is the starkest single-state disclosure gap in the file.

West Bengal: zero company-level awards sourceable. The WBIDC land dashboard publishes application and approval counts, not allottees. A reported CAG finding of a Rs 12.86 crore loss to WBIDC on a land allotment to a Flipkart logistics entity could not be fetched (404) and is therefore NOT recorded as an award.

CAG state audit reports are PDF-only. cag.gov.in offers filtering by state, sector and report type but no machine-readable data, so state audit findings on procurement cannot be systematically mined - they can only be read report by report.

City gas distribution was in the brief but yielded no state awards, and this is itself the answer: CGD geographical areas are awarded by PNGRB, a central regulator, under central bidding rounds, not by state governments. No state CGD award belongs in this file. (Gujarat's pre-PNGRB legacy CGD arrangements were not investigated in this pass.)

Much of what is loosely called a 'state renewable PPA' is in fact a central intermediary procurement by SECI, NTPC or NHPC that a state discom later signs into. Awards of that kind were excluded here; see the rejected list.

Three of Tata Power's four Odisha distribution concessions (TPNODL, TPWODL, TPSODL) are omitted for want of a fetchable source. Secondary reporting puts the TPSODL and TPWODL considerations at Rs 127.50 crore and Rs 255 crore, but we could not fetch that source and have not recorded those figures as facts.

METHOD LIMIT: the WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted at the outset, and all discovery was done by fetching search-engine result pages, several of which then rate-limited. Coverage of Gujarat, Karnataka, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh is materially thinner than of the other eight states as a direct result. Absence of awards for a state in this file reflects that constraint as much as it reflects state disclosure practice, and the two causes are not separated.
Several award dates are partial or absent because the primary source itself redacts or omits them - notably Tata Power's Solapur LoA release, published as 'March **, 2023'.

governingParty is populated from well-established public record of which party held the state government at the award date, and is null wherever the award date is null. It is a roster field for computing base rates across differently-governed states. No causal reading is drawn from it anywhere in this file, and none should be drawn downstream.

No denial or company response has been captured for the one contested row (Godda land acquisition). Under the evidence-tiering rules that row is a roster entry only and must not be used as an allegation until the company's position is recorded as a contra edge.
